subject: SLA concession proposal — CloudCart multi-region latency window
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Incident window details for CloudCart — ops summary

Lukas / team,

Quick operational summary from the SE side: between 2026-11-26T22:40 and 2026-11-27T03:10 UTC we observed sustained p95 latency spikes for CloudCart across us-west-2 and us-east-1 serving pools. Root cause: concurrent autoscaler mis-scheduling on a subset of Dedicated hosts after a kernel patch; affected 7 of their 24 capacity units.

Impact metrics (attached):
- p95 latency uplift: +320ms (baseline 190ms -> 510ms)
- error rate: remained <0.3% (no data loss)
- sustained window: ~4.5 hours total across two bursts

Customer impact: higher-than-acceptable tail latency for checkout microservices; they escalated to CS and legal for SLA recourse. CloudCart is on a committed Dedicated plan (monthly reserved capacity).

Requested: ops has produced the postmortem and a usage snapshot (attached). Sales needs an initial concession framework to present — tiered credits, one-time free month, or a blended invoice offset. My suggestion is to surface three options with RTO/RPO neutral language; ops will own the incident timeline details.

Jonas
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_postmortem.pdf (summary + timeline), cloudcart_usage_snapshot.csv (hourly tokens by region)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Incident window details for CloudCart — ops summary

Thanks Jonas — this is helpful.

Karthik, can you draft a concise external-facing concession proposal that includes:
- a baseline monetary credit (percentage of November invoice),
- a short free-month option (for a single billing cycle),
- and a blended remediation credit tied to usage (applies only to reserved capacity hours during the incident).

From a commercial perspective, we should cap the total to a number that keeps our commercial math intact but is meaningful to CloudCart. My ballpark is $60k–$140k depending on mix — include a structured fallback so Finance has a clean approval path. Also include language about accelerated ops safeguards (patch rollback timeline, extra monitoring).

I will prepare the external note once you give me the three-line options.

— Lukas
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-29T14:45:00-08:00
Subject: Draft concession framework for CloudCart (for review)

Lukas / team — draft below, tidy it for tone and send when ready. I kept the options simple (A/B/C) for quick evaluation by CloudCart legal/finance.

Option A — Usage-proportional credit (preferred)- One-time credit equal to 20% of CloudCart's November reserved invoice, applied as an account credit valid for 12 months. Applies only to reserved-capacity tokens/hours recorded during the incident windows.

Option B — Free month- One free month of reserved capacity (same SKU), applied as a single billing-cycle waiver. No retroactive cash payout; credit only.

Option C — Blended cap- Blended remediation: $50k fixed credit + 10% of November reserved spend during incident hours; capped at $120k.

Additional commitments (applies to all options):
- Ops remediation: patch rollback completed, extra monitoring for 30 days.
- Root cause postmortem delivered and SLA timeline added to their account.
- If CloudCart elects cash refund rather than credit, Finance will route to Exec approval; otherwise credit applies automatically.

Need: Marissa — quick signoff on the maximum cap (I put $120k on Option C). If you confirm, Lukas should propose to the customer with the option language and next steps.

Karthik
Sr. AE, Redwood Inference

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: Ayesha Khan <ayesha.k@cloudcart.com>, contracts@cloudcart.com
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T09:30:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: remediation options following Nov 26–27 latency window

Ayesha — thank you for the patience while we completed our analysis and postmortem. I’m writing to propose three remediation options for the latency window that impacted CloudCart (summary attached). Please see the simple choices below; pick the one that works best for you and we’ll operationalize immediately.

Option A — Usage-proportional credit (recommended)- A one-time account credit equal to 20% of CloudCart's November reserved-capacity invoice, applied against future bills; credit valid for 12 months. Credit will be scoped to reserved-capacity hours impacted per the attached CSV.

Option B — One free month- One billing cycle of the reserved capacity SKU (same capacity level), applied as a waiver.

Option C — Blended remediation (cap)- $50,000 fixed account credit plus 10% of November reserved spend during incident hours, capped at $120,000.

Operational commitments- We have rolled back the kernel patch that triggered the mis-scheduling and added enhanced autoscaler safety checks. Jonas will run an independent verification task and share daily telemetry for 7 days.

If you prefer a cash refund rather than account credit, please let us know — if chosen, we will escalate for finance exec approval and follow a separate payout flow.

Next steps- Reply with A, B, or C and whether you prefer credit vs cash. We’ll then issue an account credit or route to finance for payout approval.

Apologies again for the disruption — we take uptime seriously and are committed to making this right.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Director, Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: incident_postmortem.pdf, cloudcart_usage_snapshot.csv

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-01T16:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: remediation options following Nov 26–27 latency window

Lukas / Karthik — I’ve reviewed the options and the postmortem. Approve Option C (blended remediation) as the default customer offer, capped at $120k. Rationale: it balances commercial risk and customer goodwill while keeping the remedy meaningful.

For payouts: if CloudCart asks for cash, route to me and include expected payout amount and justification memo (Karthik to prepare). Finance will need a one-page approval note; if payout >$100k I will need Exec sign-off (CEO). If they stick with account credit, sales can approve locally.

Please proceed to send the finalized offer to CloudCart. If they accept cash, Karthik, set up the approval packet and tag me.

—Marissa
VP, Commercial
Redwood Inference
